overview: Covers generation, collection, transportation, and processing of municipal solid waste; classified into Wet/Biodegradable, Dry/Non-Biodegradable, and Recyclable waste categories.
current_situation: Total waste generation ~1,389-1,451 TPD (2025), ~407 g/capita/day. 95-100% segregation at source, 100% door-to-door collection, 100% grievance redressal (ESR 2024-25). 4,432 personnel deployed across the SWM chain. SWM sector GHG emissions = 2,00,000 tCO2e (2025).

baseline_data.metric: Sanitary waste going to landfill untreated

challenges: Waste generation growth outpacing infrastructure (all currently routed to Moshi depot)
Insufficient processing capacity at MRF and mechanised windrow composting plants
Waste-to-Energy plant underperforming due to high calorific value of RDF
Wet-waste processing capacity inadequate for projected future demand
Need for additional infrastructure incl. ~150 TPD STP sludge-to-biofuel processing
10% of sanitary waste landfilled without scientific processing
Data discrepancies across reported waste quantities and facility capacities
existing_initiatives: Waste-to-Energy plant at Moshi garbage depot (14 MW electricity generation)
50 TPD bio-methanation plant (hotel/restaurant waste to biogas/bio-CNG)
5 TPD plastic-to-fuel plant (since 2010, BVG Pvt. Ltd., 20-year PPP)

strategies.name: Create and execute a long-term, detailed plan to promote circularity in SWM and enhance climate resilience.
Enhance source segregation to improve downstream processing across all categories.
Transition to cleaner fuels in waste transportation and fast-track biomining.
Use data and technology to modernise SWM (GIS, IoT bins, dashboards, AI route optimisation).
Leverage the carbon-credit market by monetising emission reductions from composting, bio-methanation, landfill diversion, WtE.
